text:
support_julie: Heads up — customer ACME reporting sudden p99 spike from EU clients since ~08:00 UTC. They see long TLS handshakes and occasional 5xx. Sending client trace and short repro.

maria_s: Thanks. Any per-pop breakdown? Is it concentrated on a single POP or spread across eu-pop-*?

support_julie: All in EU but mostly eu-pop-3 and eu-pop-5 according to their headers. Here's the curl -w timing they sent:
```
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -w "namelookup:%{time_namelookup}\nconnect:%{time_connect}\nappconnect:%{time_appconnect}\npretransfer:%{time_pretransfer}\nstarttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\ntotal:%{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
namelookup:0.012
connect:0.145
appconnect:0.922
pretransfer:0.922
starttransfer:1.035
total:1.045
```

kevin_n: appconnect ~900ms — that's the TLS handshake. Can you drop a traceroute from their client?

support_julie: They provided a traceroute showing extra hop via a partner CGNAT/edge (obfuscated):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms  0.5 ms  0.5 ms
 2  198.51.100.10  2.1 ms  2.3 ms  2.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.200  45.6 ms  46.1 ms  45.9 ms  <-- partner-cgnat
 4  203.0.113.45  46.0 ms  46.2 ms  46.1 ms
```

ingrid_netops: That intermediate hop looks like our peering partner in the region. We recently had a route weight change for eu-pop-3 last week; worth checking if traffic got redistributed through a suboptimal path.

maria_s: On our side I'm seeing elevated SYN->ACK latency and TLS handshake tails for connections terminated at eu-pop-3 between 07:50-08:20 UTC. p95 jumped from ~80ms to ~700ms. Correlating with BGP weight shift?

netbot: Alert: eu-pop-3 p99 TLS-handshake latency > 600ms (08:03 UTC) ; increased connection resets seen +12%

kevin_n: Can we reproduce quickly from an internal probe in the same AZ/region? If internal probes show same path, good signal.

maria_s: Running curl from probe eu-probe-3 now. Output:
```
appconnect:0.880
starttransfer:0.995
total:1.010
```
Looks similar.

ingrid_netops: I'm going to query our router table for any recent BGP weight/AS-path changes affecting eu-pop-3. Also opening ticket with partner to confirm whether they're seeing TLS rate-limiting or proxy buffering causing handshake delay.

maria_s: Short mitigation idea: divert a portion of user traffic off eu-pop-3 to eu-pop-2 (weight tweak) and enable extra connection reuse (keepalive tuning) on the proxy layer to reduce new-handshake load. Also increase handshake timeout threshold for the edge so transient partner slowness doesn't bubble as 5xx.

deploy-bot: route-weight update: eu-pop-3 -> weight 60, eu-pop-2 -> weight 40 (initiated by maria_s).

maria_s: Applied weight tweak. Monitoring p99 and error rate now. If p99 drops within 10m we keep the diversion and ask partner to roll fix.

support_julie: Customer confirmed reduced errors after ~6m. They still see slightly elevated tail but much improved. :relieved:

kevin_n: We'll keep working with partner and follow up with a postmortem: dig into why a CGNAT hop introduced handshake tail (NAT timeouts, buffer queuing, TLS offload mismatch). For now leave diversion in place and schedule a controlled rollback test with traffic ramp.

maria_s: Agreed. I'll track in internal incident and update the postmortem template. Closing slack thread for triage updates; keep me copied on partner ticket.

netbot: Note: create-incident -> INC-2026-478 (triage: network-partner-handshake-tail)
